rules.message: RabbitMQ 4.x removed lazy mode, the queue version and master locator arguments, and classic mirrored queues. The broker rejects the declaration or the policy.
rules.fix: Declare durable work queues with ["x-queue-type"] = "quorum". Replace ha-* policies with quorum queues.

rules.message: Quorum queues do not support global QoS, and RabbitMQ 4.3 denies it by default.
rules.fix: Set the prefetch per consumer: BasicQosAsync(0, n, global: false). Start between 10 and 100.
nomatch: await channel.BasicQosAsync(prefetchSize: 0, prefetchCount: 20, global: false, ct);

rules.message: With automatic ack, the broker forgets the message on delivery. A crash or an exception in the handler loses it.
rules.fix: Consume with autoAck: false and call BasicAckAsync after the work and the database commit.

rules.message: One IChannel for all requests mixes the frames of concurrent publishes, and one channel error stops all publishers.
rules.fix: Give each publisher its own channel with publisher confirms, or publish from one outbox BackgroundService that owns its channel.
nomatch: await using var channel = await connection.CreateChannelAsync(options, ct);

rules.message: new RabbitMqBuilder() is obsolete (CS0618) and starts rabbitmq:3.11. Tests then run on another major version than production.
rules.fix: Pin the production major version: new RabbitMqBuilder("rabbitmq:4.3-management-alpine").

rules.message: The delayed message exchange plugin keeps messages on one node without replication, and it is not part of the default broker.
rules.fix: Use a dead-letter exchange with a TTL queue, the EasyNetQ default scheduler, or Wolverine scheduled messages.

rules.message: EasyNetQ 9 is an alpha. Stay on EasyNetQ 8.x, and use Wolverine for new flows (decision MSG-04).

match: var factory = new ConnectionFactory { Uri = uri };
